prompt: A single creature sprite for RimWorld: the surrik, a large alien root-crust swimmer, rendered in a painterly, realistic vanilla RimWorld style with a clean dark outline on a transparent background. The view is the game's low three-quarter camera, the same height and scale for every facing, so the sprite stays about 108 px tall. The surrik lies low and horizontal, half-sunk in a dense, matted crust of interlaced dark twisting roots and tan-brown root-mat slabs, caught mid-glide as it swims through the crust as though through water. The root mat heaves up and splits in a bow wave in front of the massive shoulders, with torn root ends curling aside, and a closing wake furrow of settling roots trails behind the haunch; the crust is whole and unbroken around the body, thick woven root rather than ferns or leaves. Its build is an alien, heavy-shouldered swimmer: an enormous humped shoulder mass is the tallest, leading part of the silhouette and pushes through the mat, with ridged, armored plates of slate-brown hide over the shoulders. The head is sunk low beneath and behind the shoulder hump, with no neck extended. Along the head runs a wide, upturned jaw line that opens upward, an under-slung striking mouth made to snap up from beneath the crust, clearly visible from the front and the side. Small, deep-set, dark eyes sit wide apart on the low head. The body slopes down from the shoulder hump to a heavy haunch and tail sunk in the mat, the matte slate-brown hide is paler along the underside, and the limbs are smooth, short flippered stubs mostly hidden below the crust line. Front view: the eyes and upturned jaw face the viewer, the shoulder hump rising behind and above the low head. Side view: the shoulder hump is the tallest mass at the front of the body, the head sunk beneath and behind it, the bow wave ahead of the shoulders and the wake behind the haunch. Rear view, seen from behind at the same low camera angle as the front view and mirroring its framing: the rounded back of the shoulders and haunches rises out of the mat, the tail end toward the viewer, foreshortened, as wide and low as the front view, with the eyes hidden. The crust uses the same tan-brown slabs and dark roots throughout.
